metais sample — Generate sample data from the inputs' schemas, and keep it as a
data directory or an example.

Usage:
  metais sample [<package>] (--out <dir> | --example <name>) [--optional <mode>]
                [--seed <n>] [--items <n>] [supply flags] [--overwrite]
                [--dry-run] [--json]

Examples:
  metais sample --out data
      Writes sample data for the source directory in the working directory into
      the new directory data.
  metais sample report-1.0.0.metais --out data --seed 7 --optional mixed
      Writes other data, with some optional fields left out.
  metais sample --example staged --set /incident/stage=final
      Saves data whose stage is final as the example staged.
  metais sample --out data --overwrite --json
      Replaces the data files in data, and lists them as one metais.sample/1
      document.

The generator makes a value for every input from its schema: the schema's const,
examples, default or enum where it has one, and otherwise placeholder text,
numbers and dates of its own. Values given with --set, --set-json and
--inputs-json are fixed points: they are kept as given, conditionals evaluated
against them, and only what they leave out is made. The same package, options,
supplied values and seed give the same data on every platform.

The data is written as a data directory, one file per input in its first form
and one directory per collection, and is read back and validated exactly as
metais render --data reads it, before anything is written. A field the generator
cannot make a valid value for is schema.sample_unsatisfiable, and data that
fails its schema, such as a supplied value the schema refuses, is
schema.sample_invalid; with any error nothing is written.

With --out, the data directory is <dir>: a <dir> that does not exist is created,
with its missing parents, beside it and renamed into place; an empty one is
written into. A <dir> that holds any entry, a hidden one included, is refused
unless --overwrite is given, and then each file sample writes replaces the file
of that name, and nothing else in <dir> is read, changed or removed. Everything
sample writes into an existing <dir>, an empty collection's directory included,
is prepared beneath <dir>/.metais-staging and moved into place. A link, a
directory or a special file where sample writes a file, a file where it needs a
directory, and a name that differs only in case from one it writes are each
refused, all of them together, before anything is written.

With --example, the source directory's examples/<name>/ is written: its inputs/
holds the data, and its example.yaml records how it was made. It is refused with
a packed package, and when examples/<name>/ exists at all; nothing in an example
is ever replaced. --dry-run lists the files and writes nothing.

Operands:
  <package>
      A source directory, or a packed package file with --out; the current
      directory when omitted. - is refused, since a package is read with random
      access.

Flags:
  --out <dir>
      The directory to write the data directory into: one that does not exist
      yet, or an empty one, or with --overwrite any directory.
  --example <name>
      Save the data as the inputs of a new example, examples/<name>/, of the
      source directory.
  --optional <mode>
      Which optional properties and inputs the generator makes: all of them,
      none (and null wherever null is allowed), or a mix the seed decides.
      Values: all, none, mixed. Default: all.
  --seed <n>
      The generator's seed, an unsigned 64-bit integer: the same package,
      options, supplied values and seed give the same data. Default: 0.
  --items <n>
      The number of items the generator aims for in every array and collection,
      within the schema's bounds. Default: 3.
  --set <pointer>=<text>
      Set one value at an inputs pointer, such as /vendor/name=Acme; the text is
      coerced to the type the schema declares there. Applied after --data and
      --inputs-json, in command-line order with --set-json. May be given more
      than once.
  --set-json <pointer>=<json>
      Set one value at an inputs pointer as JSON text, the way to set null, an
      array or an object. Applied in command-line order with --set. May be given
      more than once.
  --inputs-json <json>
      A JSON object whose members are inputs, each replacing that input's whole
      value; - reads it from standard input, once. Applied after --data, in
      command-line order. May be given more than once.
  --overwrite
      With --out, write into a directory that holds entries, replacing the files
      sample writes and nothing else.
  --dry-run
      Generate and validate the data, list the files sample would write, and
      write nothing.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  The files written, relative to <dir> or to examples/<name>/, in path order; an
  empty directory, a collection with no item, is listed with a trailing /. With
  --json, one metais.sample/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits
  output.destination.case_variant
      In <dir>, an entry's name differs only in case or normalization from a
      name a path sample writes holds.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  output.destination.commit_failed
      Moving the files into an existing <dir> failed part way; the files already
      moved are listed, and nothing else was changed.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  output.destination.link
      In <dir>, a path sample writes runs through, or ends at, a symbolic link,
      a junction or another reparse point, which is never followed.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  output.destination.not_directory
      --out, or a directory above it, exists and is not a directory; or, in
      <dir>, a file stands where a path sample writes needs a directory.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  output.destination.not_empty
      --out names a directory that holds entries, and --overwrite is not given.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir> --overwrite
  output.destination.not_regular_file
      In <dir>, a directory, a named pipe, a socket or a device stands where
      sample writes a file.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  output.destination.nothing_written
      A write failed, another file system is mounted on a path sample writes, or
      the example already exists; nothing is left written.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  output.destination.staging_exists
      <dir> holds .metais-staging, left by a killed write or in use by another;
      nothing is written.
      Next: metais sample <package> --out <dir>
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.bad_value
      --seed or --items is not a whole number in range, or --example is not a
      name an example can have.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.conflicting_flags
      --inputs-json - is given twice, and standard input is read once.
      Next: metais help inputs
  usage.flag_excluded
      --out and --example are both given, or --overwrite is given with
      --example.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.not_a_source_directory
      --example is given with a packed package, whose examples are not edited.
      Next: metais unpack <package> --out <dir>
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais sample --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais sample --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals sample' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  collection.* (5)    A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  csv.* (7)           A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  input.* (52)        A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  json.* (5)          A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  limit.exceeded (1)  A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused (exceeded). Next: metais inspect <package>
  manifest.* (44)     The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                      Next: metais inspect <package>
  markdown.* (3)      A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  package.* (47)      The package is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (10)       An input schema is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (2)        The generated data cannot be made or does not validate.
                      Next: metais schema <package> <name>
  template.* (9)      An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                      Next: metais inspect <package>
  yaml.* (13)         A value given with --set, --set-json or --inputs-json is
                      refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
